title: Add a package-independent deterministic lifecycle helper
summary: A single shared lifecycle helper (packaging/lifecycle.sh) provides six typed phases — pre-install, post-install, pre-upgrade, post-upgrade, pre-remove, post-remove — used by all three distro package hooks (Arch .install, Fedora .spec, Debian postinst/prerm/postrm). The helper validates model layout + sha256 hashes against model-manifest.toml, verifies identities/dirs (sysusers, tmpfiles, /var/lib/namtor, /run/namtor), socket + D-Bus service units, and the PAM module. It drives `namtor-pam-edit` as a subprocess for snapshot (pre-upgrade), migrate (post-upgrade), disable-all (pre-remove), and purge (post-remove). It emits a deterministic receipt per phase. PAM is default-off: post-install and pre-install never call namtor-pam-edit and never write under /etc/pam.d. The helper is idempotent and fake-root testable via --root <DESTDIR>; systemd/desktop-cache invocations are skipped on fake roots so the suite runs without root or a running systemd.

phases.pre-install: register sysusers + tmpfiles; verify prerequisite config files are staged under --root. Never edits PAM.
phases.post-install: validate model layout/hashes, identities/dirs, socket + D-Bus units, PAM module; update desktop caches; enable socket. Emit receipt. Never edits PAM.
phases.pre-upgrade: snapshot PAM state via `namtor-pam-edit snapshot`; stop the daemon. Never edits PAM lines.
phases.post-upgrade: migrate PAM via `namtor-pam-edit migrate`; re-validate model layout/hashes + services. Emit receipt.
phases.pre-remove: disable all PAM services via `namtor-pam-edit disable-all`; stop the daemon.
phases.post-remove: purge all PAM state via `namtor-pam-edit purge`; remove runtime dirs. Emit receipt.

assertions.all_six_phases_accepted_on_complete_root: PASS — pre-install, post-install, pre-upgrade, post-upgrade, pre-remove, post-remove all exit 0 on a complete fake root
assertions.post_install_emits_receipt: PASS — <root>/var/lib/namtor/lifecycle/post-install.receipt written with phase, version, root, status, checks_total/passed/failed, pam_edited, models_validated
assertions.post_install_no_pam_edit: PASS — post-install does not invoke namtor-pam-edit (PAM default-off)
assertions.mandatory_failure_missing_models: PASS — post-install returns nonzero when /var/lib/namtor/models is empty
assertions.mandatory_failure_missing_sysusers: PASS — post-install returns nonzero when sysusers.d/namtor.conf is absent
assertions.mandatory_failure_missing_service_unit: PASS — post-install returns nonzero when namtor-daemon.service is absent
assertions.mandatory_failure_missing_dbus: PASS — post-install returns nonzero when org.namtor.Manager.service is absent
assertions.mandatory_failure_missing_pam_module: PASS — post-install returns nonzero when pam_namtor.so is absent
assertions.mandatory_failure_tampered_model: PASS — post-install returns nonzero when an onnx file's sha256 does not match the manifest variant
assertions.idempotent: PASS — running post-install twice yields the same exit code (0) and the same receipt content (ignoring the timestamp field)
assertions.fake_root_honoured: PASS — receipt and validation operate under --root <DESTDIR>; the real /var/lib/namtor is untouched
assertions.post_remove_purges_runtime_dirs: PASS — /var/lib/namtor/models removed under the fake root
assertions.no_nonexistent_cli: PASS — lifecycle.sh contains no `models ensure` or `namtor-cli models` reference
assertions.no_pam_editing_in_post_install_body: PASS — the namtor_lc_phase_post_install function body contains no pam-edit enable/disable/migrate/snapshot/purge or /etc/pam.d reference
assertions.no_pam_editing_in_pre_install_body: PASS — the namtor_lc_phase_pre_install function body contains no PAM editing
assertions.arch_install_invokes_lifecycle: PASS — packaging/arch/namtor.install references lifecycle.sh with a typed phase
assertions.fedora_spec_invokes_lifecycle: PASS — packaging/fedora/namtor.spec references lifecycle.sh with a typed phase
assertions.debian_scripts_invoke_lifecycle: PASS — at least one Debian maintainer script references lifecycle.sh with a typed phase
assertions.arch_delegates_pam: PASS — Arch .install contains no direct namtor-pam-edit snapshot/migrate/disable-all/purge call
assertions.fedora_delegates_pam: PASS — Fedora .spec contains no direct namtor-pam-edit snapshot/migrate/disable-all/purge call
assertions.debian_postinst_delegates_pam: PASS — Debian postinst contains no direct pam-edit lifecycle call
assertions.debian_prerm_delegates_pam: PASS — Debian prerm contains no direct pam-edit lifecycle call
assertions.debian_postrm_delegates_pam: PASS — Debian postrm contains no direct pam-edit lifecycle call

arch.pre_install: not called (pacman has not extracted the payload yet; the helper is not on disk)

debian.postrm_remove: light tmpfiles cleanup only (keep user state for reinstall)
debian.postrm_upgrade: lifecycle.sh post-upgrade (new payload already on disk)

post_remove_cache_invariant: pacman, RPM, and dpkg all delete the package payload BEFORE the final post-remove hook runs. The distro hooks cache /usr/share/namtor/lifecycle.sh to /var/tmp/namtor-lifecycle.sh in pre-remove so post-remove can still invoke it. The cache is removed after post-remove completes.

manifest_resolution.repo_fallback: packaging/model-manifest.toml — used ONLY on a real root (--root /); suppressed on fake roots so test fixtures with arbitrary weights are not validated against the production manifest's hashes
manifest_resolution.presence_only: if no manifest is resolvable, validate_models falls back to requiring at least one .onnx under the models dir
